description: This radial chart visually organizes medical ethics principles into three primary categories—Beneficence, Autonomy, and Justice—each represented by a distinct colored segment. The largest segment, labeled “Beneficence,” is a medium blue and contains twelve subcategories including “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” and “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients.” Adjacent to it, the “Justice” segment is a muted reddish-brown and includes subcategories like “Promote Environmental Sustainability,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” and “Prevent Patient from Harm.” The third main category, “Autonomy,” is a muted green and includes subcategories such as “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve,” “Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication,” and “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed.” Each subcategory is presented as a thin wedge radiating outward from its respective main category, with labels written along the arc of the chart. The chart does not include percentage values, a legend, or any visual emphasis such as exploded slices; the segments appear to be arranged in descending order of size within each main category, with the largest subcategory within Beneficence being “Provide Medical Care to Patients.”
